user_goal: Create a general CPU-only quantum-computing emulator for JANUS and search for independently verifiable future-to-past signals without a QPU.

implementation.engine: Classical CPU-only adaptive circuit interpreter. Stim for Clifford; NumPy complex128 for circuits containing non-Clifford T; no physical quantum hardware.

architecture_inspiration.name: Qiskit Aer
architecture_inspiration.feature: Adaptive backends: statevector, density matrix, stabilizer, matrix product state

architecture_inspiration.name: Google qsim
architecture_inspiration.feature: Vectorization and gate fusion; not yet added to R1

test_classes: independent Stim vs NumPy 6-qubit observable comparisons
forbidden future manipulation of early register rejected

largest_verified_clifford_case.timing_note: From Python 3.12 GitHub worker log, only engine time, not full CI; not an apples-to-apples speedup vs old 16-qubit Python script.

scientific_boundary.why: A CPU emulating the quantum state implements classical rules in ordinary time. An unknown independently generated late bit cannot be obtained by running those rules without a physical resource or information leak. Outputs may validate a mathematical retrocausal hypothesis but cannot independently prove a physical channel.

next_milestones: R2: introduce additional backends (Qiskit Aer MPS or qsim), conditioned on workload metrics and independent reference tests.
R3: specify and search hypothetical non-CPTP/CTC/process-matrix candidates with exact accounting for normalization and leak/selection controls; record mathematical-only labels.
R4: freeze every real prior CPU generated candidate's *early* bit prediction, obtain independent late entropy in a separate externally sealed stage, verify all unselected trials, and retain controls.
R5: require physically authenticated timing, independent replication and no classical leakage before any physical retrocausal signal claim.

candidate_validation.structural_guard: Late branch gates cannot touch earlier registered qubits in simulated chronology.
